- Overestimate prices in bullish sentiment periods; reduce forecast peaks when sentiment is high or trending upward.
- Underestimate prices after sharp declines; model should anticipate mean reversion toward prior range, especially when sentiment is low or neutral.
- Overshoot after recent spikes; cap forecast peaks at 1–2% below prior high or 1.5x recent average if sentiment is cooling.
- Lag in downward corrections: if sentiment drops sharply, model should adjust downward 1–2 days before true price drop.
- Avoid overfitting to recent highs; if sentiment is weak or negative, reduce forecast volatility and anchor to 3–5 day moving average.
- When sentiment is consistently low or negative, forecast should be 5–10% below historical mean of last 10–15 days.
- If sentiment is rising but price is falling, model should not overreact — reduce forecast slope to avoid “sentiment-driven overcorrection.”
